generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential from 1; never NULL; unique per table; generated PKs start above compact maxima.
generic_sampling_rules.smallint_unsigned: Uniform integer in [1, 32767]; never NULL for NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.tinyint_unsigned: Uniform integer in [1, 255]; never NULL for NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.mediumint_unsigned: Uniform integer in [1, 8388607]; never NULL for NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random uppercase word from a 200-word pool, length 3-20; near-variants (case, trailing space) for equality/LIKE targets.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_long: Random sentence 20-120 chars from a template pool.
generic_sampling_rules.text: Random sentence 40-200 chars; occasional near-duplicate of another row's text.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_money: Uniform in [0.00, 99.99] rounded to 2 decimals; boundary values at listed literals plus one step (0.01) on each side, mixed with uniform draws (boundary probability 0.2).
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_rate: Uniform in [0.00, 9.99] rounded to 2 decimals; boundary values at listed literals plus one step (0.01) on each side, mixed with uniform draws (boundary probability 0.2).
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform timestamp in [2005-05-24 00:00:00, 2006-02-15 23:59:59], format %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S; duplicates allowed on DISTINCT-target columns.
generic_sampling_rules.timestamp: Constant 2006-02-15 04:00:00 unless a column is a DISTINCT target; then vary by seconds.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_special_features: Random subset of ('Trailers','Commentaries','Deleted Scenes','Behind the Scenes') joined by comma, or NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, use the compact database's NULL share; if that share is 0.0, plant at least one NULL row per instance (share >= 1/n) unless the spec overrides the share; NOT NULL and primary-key columns never get NULL; clamp planted NULLs to at most n-1 so at least one non-NULL row remains unless an explicit 100%-NULL exception is documented.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values: Text columns draw fresh values with 80% probability, reuse an existing value with 20% to create duplicates/ties.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: For columns marked duplicates_for_distinct, with probability duplicate_share reuse a previously drawn value; applies to NumberSampler, WordSampler, StringSampler and DateSampler.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: For each parent/child FK pair marked unmatched_join_rows, after generating child FKs, remove all children of at least one chosen parent row so that parent has no children; child FK columns are never NULL. Identify removed child rows by full primary-key tuple (not pk_cols[0]); remove or re-point all transitive dependents in dependency order before the final FK-repair pass; a final FK-repair pass re-validates the whole chain.
generic_sampling_rules.ties_for_order_limit: For each column marked ties_for_order_limit, explicitly assign at least two child rows to the same parent (the one with the highest count) so that ordering by COUNT(*) DESC has a tie at rank 1; only existing parent keys are used; the target is mapped to the child FK column that produces the COUNT(*) grouping.
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary: For each column marked aggregate_boundary, explicitly construct child counts per parent to hit the listed target values (e.g., 2, 3, 4, 29, 30, 31) for the relevant join; only existing parent keys are used and no parent PK is mutated; size the child table to at least sum(targets); construct deterministically on distinct parents; apply after FK repair or make FK repair preserve already-valid values; assert realized per-parent counts include the target values.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: For each column marked group_sizes, explicitly assign distinct values to form one group of size 1, one of size 2 and one of size >= 3 among the column's values; for FK columns choose distinct existing parent keys; verify the resulting group-size multiset contains 1, 2 and >=3. Never rewrite primary-key columns; for FK columns only reuse values that exist in the parent table.
generic_sampling_rules.comparison_boundary: For each column marked comparison_boundary, explicitly assign at least one child row whose FK equals a parent key and one whose FK is one step from a parent key in the parent's key ordering (skip the one-step value if no such parent exists); never use arithmetic p+/-1 that may not exist.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_repair: After all constructions, run a final FK-repair pass: every child FK value must reference an existing parent key; if not, re-point to an existing parent key or drop the row. Enable foreign_keys=ON (or run an explicit FK validation query) and treat any FK violation as a unit failure. Iterate over flattened table names only; never let repair mutate values deliberately set by pattern constructors; run repair before pattern construction or make constructors FK-safe by construction.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `build_random_instance` calls `_copy_columns(spec, schema, t, inst)` for every table in `order`, but `_copy_columns` only handles `spec['copy_columns'][table]` keyed by child column name. For `film_text`, the spec's `copy_columns` maps `film_id -> film.film_id`, `title -> film.title`, `description -> film.description`. Inside `_copy_columns`, for each child_col it does `fk = schema.fks.get((table, child_col))` and skips when `fk is None`. `film_text.film_id` is a PK and FK to `film.film_id`, so `fk` exists for `film_id`, but for `title` and `description` there is no FK entry, so those columns are skipped and remain randomly sampled. The semantic rule `film_text.title = film.title VIA film_text.film_id` and `film_text.description = film.description VIA film_text.film_id` is therefore not enforced. Execution feedback shows `film_text.description: generated rows: NULL 77 / 3895` while `film.description: NULL 55 / 5251`, confirming the copy is not happening (counts differ and title/description are not derived from film).
issues.requested_revision: Fix `_copy_columns` so that for a table with a copy spec, the FK column (e.g. `film_text.film_id`) is used to look up the parent row, and all copied columns (`title`, `description`) are filled from the parent row keyed by that FK. Alternatively, in `build_random_instance`, after generating `film_text.film_id`, set `title`/`description` from `inst['film']` by matching `film_id`. Ensure the copied columns are not independently sampled.

issues.evidence: The spec's `null_targets` includes `film.original_language_id` with `null_share: 100%`, and the program's `_null_share` returns `spec['null_shares'][key]` = 1.0 for that column. Execution feedback confirms `film.original_language_id: generated rows: NULL 5251 / 5251` — 100% NULL. However, the spec's `per_column_exceptions` also lists `film.original_language_id` with `null_share: 100%`, which is consistent. But the spec's `null_targets` also lists `film.rating`, `film.release_year`, `film.special_features`, `film.length`, `film.description` as nullable targets, and the program plants NULLs in them (feedback shows 55/5251 each). The spec's `null_share` rule says 'For each nullable column, 1-2% NULL rows (at least one) unless statistics show 0% NULL; then 0 NULLs.' The program's `_null_share` uses the compact database's share when no spec override exists. For `film.rating`, `film.release_year`, etc., the compact DB likely has 0% NULL (they are NOT NULL in schema? Actually `film.rating` has no NOT NULL in schema, `film.release_year` is nullable, `film.special_features` nullable). The spec's `null_targets` lists them, so planting NULLs is allowed. This is not an error per se, but the spec's `null_share` rule says 'unless statistics show 0% NULL; then 0 NULLs' — the program does not check statistics for 0% NULL; it uses `max(share, 1/len(vals))` which forces at least one NULL even when the compact DB has 0% NULL. This contradicts the spec's rule. Evidence: `_null_share` in instance.py: `return max(share, 1.0 / max(1, len(vals)))` — always at least one NULL. The spec says 'unless statistics show 0% NULL; then 0 NULLs.'
issues.requested_revision: In `_null_share`, if the compact database's share is 0.0 (no NULLs in original values), return 0.0 instead of forcing `1/len(vals)`. Only plant NULLs when the spec explicitly overrides the share (e.g., `address.address2: 0.7%`, `film.original_language_id: 100%`) or when the compact DB has a non-zero NULL share. This aligns with the spec's `null_share` rule.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.original_language_id` with `null_share: 100%`, but the spec's `null_targets` also lists it. The spec's `null_share` rule says 'For each nullable column, 1-2% NULL rows (at least one) unless statistics show 0% NULL; then 0 NULLs.' A 100% NULL share for `film.original_language_id` contradicts the general 1-2% rule unless justified by statistics. The spec's `uncertainty` section does not mention this. The schema shows `film.original_language_id` is nullable with no NOT NULL, but the compact database's actual NULL share is unknown from the provided evidence. The spec's `supporting_evidence` does not mention `film.original_language_id`. This is an unsupported/uncertain rule.
issues.requested_revision: Either provide evidence that `film.original_language_id` is 100% NULL in the compact database (e.g., statistics showing 0 non-NULL rows), or change the spec to a 1-2% NULL share consistent with the general rule. Document the justification in `supporting_evidence`.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `customer.create_date` with `datetime` targets `['2006-02-14 22:04:36', '2006-02-14 22:04:37']`, but the spec's `datetime` rule says 'Uniform timestamp in [2005-05-24 00:00:00, 2006-02-15 23:59:59]'. The program's `_window_for` returns that window for `customer.create_date`, and `DateSampler` draws uniformly from it. The two specific timestamps are not guaranteed to appear. The spec's `supporting_evidence` says 'Shown values 2006-02-14 22:04:36/37' — these are observed values, not a generation target. issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.rating` and `film.special_features` as `enum` targets. The program's `_domain_for` returns `('enum', ...)` for these keys, and `StringSampler._domain_value` returns a random enum value. However, the spec's `null_targets` also lists `film.rating` and `film.special_features`, and the program plants NULLs in them (feedback: 55/5251 each). The spec's `enum` rule says 'Random from (...)' — it does not mention NULLs. The general `null_share` rule allows 1-2% NULLs for nullable columns, so planting NULLs is allowed, but the spec's `enum` targets should be the primary domain. The program's `_null_share` forces at least one NULL even when the compact DB has 0% NULL (see issue 2). This is a consistency concern, not a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec whether `film.rating` and `film.special_features` should have NULLs (they are nullable in schema). If yes, keep the 1-2% NULL share; if no, remove them from `null_targets`. Ensure the program's `_null_share` respects the spec's 0% NULL rule (issue 2).

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `staff.first_name` with `comparison_boundary` targets `['Elsa', 'elsa']`. issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.language_id` and `payment.payment_date` with `duplicates_for_distinct` targets `duplicate_share: 20-50%`. The program's `_init_sampler` passes `duplicate_share=float(spec.get('duplicate_shares', {}).get(key, 0.0))`. The spec's `duplicate_shares` in `spec.py` `_EVIDENCE` has `film.language_id: 0.35`, `payment.payment_date: 0.35`, `customer.first_name: 0.35`. These are within 20-50%. However, the spec's `per_column_exceptions` also lists `customer.first_name` with `duplicates_for_distinct` targets `duplicate_share: 20-50%`, and the program's `_EVIDENCE` has `customer.first_name: 0.35`. This is consistent. But the spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.language_id` and `payment.payment_date` as `duplicates_for_distinct`, while the program's `DateSampler` for `payment.payment_date` uses `duplicate_share` to reuse fresh values with probability 0.35. The `NumberSampler` for `film.language_id` does not use `duplicate_share` at all — it ignores the parameter. Evidence: `NumberSampler.__init__` does not accept `duplicate_share`; `_init_sampler` passes it to `make_column_sampler`, which passes it to `DateSampler` only for date types. For `film.language_id` (TINYINT UNSIGNED), `make_column_sampler` returns `NumberSampler` without `duplicate_share`. So the duplicate share for `film.language_id` is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Implement `duplicate_share` in `NumberSampler` (and `StringSampler`/`WordSampler` if needed) so that with probability `duplicate_share` a previously drawn value is reused. Alternatively, document that `duplicate_share` only applies to date columns and remove it from `film.language_id` in the spec.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `actor.actor_id` and `film_actor.actor_id` with `unmatched_join_rows` targets `parent_rows_without_children: true, child_rows_with_null_fk: false`. The program's `build_random_instance` generates `film_actor.actor_id` by `fill_foreign_keys_consistently`, which draws from `instance['actor']['actor_id']` with replacement. This does not guarantee that some actor rows have no film_actor children. The spec's `unmatched_join_rows` pattern requires parent rows without children. The program does not enforce this. Execution feedback shows `construction_pairs: eligible 96, separated 23` — many pairs not separated. The `unmatched_join_rows` pattern is not implemented by construction. Evidence: `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` uses `rng.choice(pv)` for all n rows; with n=230 and parent size ~200, some parents may be missed by chance, but not guaranteed. The spec's `unmatched_join_rows` targets are not explicitly constructed.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.film_id` with `ties_for_order_limit` targets `tie_at_rank: [1], direction: DESC, tie_on: ['COUNT(*)']`. The program's `build_random_instance` generates `film.film_id` as sequential fresh keys (`start + i`), so each film_id is unique. The `ties_for_order_limit` pattern requires ties at rank 1 when ordering by `COUNT(*)` (presumably over a join like `film_actor`). Since `film_actor.film_id` is drawn with replacement from `film.film_id`, multiple film_actor rows can reference the same film, creating ties in `COUNT(*)`. However, the program does not explicitly construct a tie at rank 1; it relies on random chance. The spec's `ties_for_order_limit` target is not guaranteed. Execution feedback does not show tie verification. Evidence: `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` uses `rng.choice(pv)`; with 230 film_actor rows and ~230 films, the distribution of counts is random. A tie at rank 1 is possible but not constructed.
issues.requested_revision: In `build_random_instance`, for `film_actor.film_id`, explicitly assign at least two film_actor rows to the same film (the one with the highest count) to guarantee a tie at rank 1 when ordering by `COUNT(*) DESC`. Alternatively, document that the tie is probabilistic and adjust the spec's `ties_for_order_limit` target to reflect that.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `film.film_id` with `aggregate_boundary` targets `values: [2, 3, 4, 29, 30, 31]`. issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `payment.amount` with `comparison_boundary` targets `values: [9.99, 10.0, 10.01]`. issues.evidence: Execution feedback: every one of the 20 instances is invalid with new_integrity_failures; 1339 FK violations total. Dominant violation: film_category.category_id -> category.category_id (1297 rows across all 20 instances), plus rental.inventory_id -> inventory.inventory_id (42 rows, 18 instances). rows_skipped shows category 140 and film_category 515 rows rejected by the writer, confirming FK values point at non-existent parents.
issues.requested_revision: Fix FK generation so child FK values always reference existing parent rows. Root cause: _construct_group_sizes rewrites category.category_id values (and address.city_id, film_category.category_id) to duplicate existing values, but category.category_id is a primary key of category and film_category.category_id is a FK to it; rewriting PK values in the parent (category) breaks the child FK references, and rewriting film_category.category_id directly produces values not present in category. The group_sizes construction must not mutate primary-key or FK columns of the parent; it should only create groups on non-key columns (e.g. actor.first_name, film.title) or, for FK columns, only reuse values that exist in the parent. Similarly _construct_comparison_boundaries sets rental.customer_id to p+1/p-1 which may not exist in customer, and _construct_aggregate_boundaries/_construct_ties assign child FKs to parents but the inventory/rental chain must be re-validated after all constructions. Add a final FK-repair pass (or restrict constructions to valid parent keys) so no new FK violation is introduced.

issues.evidence: instance.py _construct_group_sizes: `out[3] = out[0] ... out[6] = out[2]` applied to keys listed in spec group_sizes, which includes 'category.category_id', 'address.city_id', 'film_category.category_id'. category.category_id is the PK of category; overwriting it with a duplicate of another row's value creates duplicate PKs in category (writer then skips 140 category rows) and orphans film_category rows. film_category.category_id is a FK; overwriting it with an arbitrary existing category value is fine only if that value exists in category, but combined with the category PK corruption it does not.
issues.requested_revision: Exclude primary-key columns and FK columns from the group_sizes rewrite, or implement group_sizes only on the value domain of non-key columns. For FK columns, group sizes should be realized by choosing among existing parent keys, never by inventing values.

issues.evidence: instance.py _construct_comparison_boundaries sets `children[1] = p + 1` and `children[2] = p - 1` for customer.customer_id (FK rental.customer_id). p+1/p-1 need not be an existing customer_id, producing rental.customer_id FK violations. The spec target is 'equal_and_one_step_from' but the construction must still reference existing parent keys.
issues.requested_revision: For comparison boundaries on FK columns, pick an existing parent key p and an existing parent key that is one step away in the parent's key ordering (or skip the one-step value if no such parent exists), rather than arithmetic p±1 that may not exist.

issues.evidence: rental.inventory_id -> inventory.inventory_id violations (42 rows, 18 instances). _construct_aggregate_boundaries for inventory.inventory_id reassigns inventory rows' PKs? No — it reassigns the child FK column of the join, but the aggregate_boundaries key 'inventory.inventory_id' is treated as a child FK (t,c) and schema.fks[(inventory, inventory_id)] does not exist, so it is skipped; however _construct_unmatched_join removes inventory rows (children of film) after rental rows were already generated referencing them, orphaning rental.inventory_id. The unmatched_join on inventory.film_id drops inventory rows without re-checking rental references.
issues.requested_revision: When removing child rows for unmatched_join (e.g. inventory rows to make a film childless), also remove or re-point dependent rows (rental referencing those inventory rows), or perform unmatched-join removal before generating grandchildren and re-validate the full FK chain. Add a final integrity check that fails the unit if any FK is violated.

issues.evidence: writer.py sets `pragma foreign_keys = OFF` and inserts with executemany, so FK violations are never detected at write time; the stats report rows_ok for all tables despite 1339 FK violations. The program reports n_ok 20, n_fail 0 while 0 of 20 instances are valid.
issues.requested_revision: Enable foreign_keys=ON (or run an explicit FK validation query after commit) and treat any FK violation as a unit failure so the reported n_ok reflects validity. Do not silently accept rows that violate declared FKs.

issues.evidence: Specification lists group_sizes targets for 'category.category_id', 'address.city_id', 'film_category.category_id' — columns that are primary keys or foreign keys. Group-size patterns on a PK are meaningless (PKs are unique by definition) and on an FK they conflict with referential integrity unless restricted to existing parent keys. The atomic-operation extraction shows group_sizes on category.category_id and film_category.category_id, which cannot be satisfied without breaking uniqueness/FK constraints.
issues.requested_revision: Remove PK columns from group_sizes targets and clarify that FK-column group_sizes must be realized only over existing parent keys. Keep group_sizes on non-key text columns (actor.first_name, actor.last_name, film.title, film.description) where it is well-defined.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units fail with TypeError("unhashable type: 'list'") at tscore_gen/instance.py:446 (`if t not in inst:`), reached from build_random_instance -> _repair_fks. In _repair_fks the loop `for t in [x for lvl in schema.table_order for x in lvl]` iterates over table names, but the preceding dead loop `for t in schema.table_order: ... for t in lvl:` rebinds `t` to a level list; more importantly the first loop `for t in schema.table_order: if t not in inst:` iterates over *levels* (lists) rather than table names, so `t not in inst` raises TypeError because a list is unhashable. Result: n_ok 0, n_fail 20, zero instances written.
issues.requested_revision: Fix _repair_fks to iterate over table names only (flatten schema.table_order once, e.g. `for t in [x for lvl in schema.table_order for x in lvl]:`), remove the dead nested loop that rebinds `t`, and re-run so that all units produce FK-consistent instances. The FK-repair pass must not raise on any schema.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_construct_unmatched_join` removes child rows of a chosen parent, but the spec's unmatched_join list includes `film_actor.actor_id` and `actor.actor_id` (same FK pair) and `inventory.film_id`; the removal drops film_actor/inventory rows but does not re-point or remove dependent `rental` rows referencing removed inventory rows in all cases (it only handles direct dependents via `_dependent_tables`, and `_drop_rows` is applied per dependent table but the child PK used to identify removed rows is `pk_cols[0]`, which for composite PKs like film_actor (actor_id, film_id) is actor_id, not a unique row identifier). This can remove the wrong rows or leave dangling grandchildren, which the final `_repair_fks` then silently re-points, defeating the intended unmatched-join construction.
issues.requested_revision: Identify removed child rows by full primary-key tuple (not pk_cols[0]) and remove/re-point all transitive dependents in dependency order before the final FK-repair pass, so the unmatched-join pattern survives validation rather than being overwritten by _repair_fks.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_construct_aggregate_boundaries` assigns `assigned.extend([p] * int(targets[i]))` for the first len(targets) parents, then truncates to len(children). With table sizes ~230 children and 230 parents, only the first few parents get the target counts and the rest get one random child each; the listed targets [2,3,4,29,30,31] for film.film_id and [2,3,4] for city/country/inventory are not reliably realized because the assignment is truncated and shuffled, and `_repair_fks`/`_construct_ties` run afterward and can overwrite these counts. The construction is not verified against the target values.
issues.requested_revision: Construct child counts deterministically to hit each listed target value on distinct parents, size the child table to at least sum(targets), and order the construction steps so ties/aggregate boundaries are applied after FK repair (or make FK repair preserve already-valid values). Add an assertion/stat that the realized per-parent counts include the target values.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_construct_group_sizes` for non-key columns does `out[3]=out[0]; out[4]=out[1]; out[5]=out[2]; out[6]=out[2]`, which only creates a group of size 2 (indices 0,3) and 3 (indices 2,5,6) if the original values at 0,1,2 happen to be distinct; it does not guarantee groups of size 1, 2 and >=3. For FK columns it picks random parent values a,b,cval that may coincide, so the required group-size profile is not guaranteed. Also `film.title`/`film.description` are non-key but the rewrite can collide with existing values.
issues.requested_revision: Explicitly assign distinct values to form one group of size 1, one of size 2 and one of size >=3 (choosing distinct parent keys for FK columns), and verify the resulting group-size multiset contains 1, 2 and >=3.

issues.evidence: Specification `null_shares` sets `film.original_language_id: 1.0` (100% NULL) while the interface NULL rule requires each nullable column to contain both NULL and non-NULL generated rows. The spec's own `null_targets` lists film.original_language_id and the supporting_evidence justifies 100% NULL from statistics, but this conflicts with the interface rule that every nullable column must have at least one non-NULL row. Similarly `film.release_year` is both a constant (2006) and listed in null_targets/null_shares 0.01, and `film.rating` is an enum but also in null_targets — the spec is internally inconsistent about whether these are NULL-bearing.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the NULL specification with the interface rule: either drop film.original_language_id from the 100%-NULL override (use a positive-but-<1 share so non-NULL rows exist) or explicitly document it as an allowed exception; and remove film.release_year/film.rating from null_targets if they are constants/enums that must be non-NULL, or state the intended share clearly.

issues.evidence: Specification `comparison_boundaries` for `customer.customer_id` targets `equal_and_one_step_from: [rental.customer_id]`, but the atomic-operations evidence describes this as `PRED(customer.customer_id >= rental.customer_id)` — a column-vs-column join predicate, not a literal comparison boundary. The program's `_construct_comparison_boundaries` only handles FK columns (`if (t,c) not in schema.fks: continue`), and customer.customer_id is a PK, not an FK, so this pattern is never constructed. The spec pattern is misclassified.
issues.requested_revision: Either reclassify customer.customer_id as a join/inequality pattern with a concrete construction (e.g., ensure some rental.customer_id equals and some is one step from a customer_id) implemented in the program, or remove it from comparison_boundaries if it is not a literal boundary.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_construct_ties` for `film.film_id` (ties_for_order_limit) requires a tie at rank 1 by COUNT(*) DESC, but it operates on `film_actor.film_id`? No — the key is `film.film_id`, which is a PK, not an FK, so `if (t,c) not in schema.fks: continue` skips it entirely. The tie is never constructed. The spec's ties_for_order_limit key `film.film_id` refers to the parent side of the film_actor join, but the program only handles child FK columns.
issues.requested_revision: Map the ties_for_order_limit target to the child FK column (film_actor.film_id) that produces the COUNT(*) grouping, and construct at least two child rows for the top parent so rank 1 ties; verify with a COUNT(*) DESC query.

issues.evidence: writer.py copies the compact database and appends generated rows, but `_repair_fks` re-points invalid FKs to arbitrary existing parents, which can silently destroy the deliberately constructed patterns (unmatched joins, aggregate boundaries, comparison boundaries) after they are built. The construction order in build_random_instance runs all pattern constructors and then `_repair_fks` last, so any pattern that produces a temporarily-invalid FK is overwritten rather than validated.
issues.requested_revision: Run FK repair before pattern construction, or make pattern constructors FK-safe by construction (only use existing parent keys), and add a post-construction validation that the specified patterns still hold; do not let _repair_fks mutate values that were deliberately set.

issues.evidence: values.py `_init_sampler` and `make_column_sampler`: for `film.rating` the declared type is empty in the schema (spec uncertainty notes this), so `make_column_sampler` falls to `if t == '' or t == 'blob': return StringSampler(...)`. The enum domain is passed, so enum values are drawn, but the `film.special_features` enum is a comma-joined subset per the generic rule while the spec lists it as a plain enum of single values; the program's StringSampler `_domain_value` returns a single value, not a subset. The generic_sampling_rules `enum_special_features` (random subset joined by comma) is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the special_features subset rule (random subset of the four features joined by comma, or NULL) in the sampler or a dedicated constructor, and confirm film.rating enum is applied despite the empty declared type.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_plant_nulls` is applied to every nullable column with `share > 0 or not cm.notnull`, and for share<=0 it plants exactly 1 NULL. But `_null_share` returns 0.0 for nullable columns not in spec.null_shares and with no original values, and the condition `if share > 0 or not cm.notnull` then plants 1 NULL — good. However, for `film.original_language_id` share=1.0, `_plant_nulls` sets k=min(round(1.0*n),n)=n, i.e. all NULL, violating the interface rule that each nullable column must also have non-NULL rows. This is the same conflict as the designer issue but manifests in code.
issues.requested_revision: Clamp the planted NULL count to at most n-1 for nullable columns so at least one non-NULL row remains, unless the spec explicitly documents a 100%-NULL exception.
